oxidation: thiolase reaction joins two acetate units.
A third acetyl-CoA is incorporated in the second step.

Formation of Ketone Bodies: Generating Free CoA

p:cNvPr.descr: PART 1: An illustration showing the formation of ketone bodies from acetyl-CoA. At the top is 2 acetyl-CoA, where C bonds left to CH3, down and right to S-CoA, and double bonds up and right to O (all in a pink box). To the right is a plus sign. To the right of this, is the same molecule, only not in a red box. Below this are reversible arrows, identified as thiolase (in blue), and pointing to acetoacetyl-CoA. The down arrow has another arrow jetting off to CoA-SH in a pink box). Acetoacetyl-CoA begins with C, which bonds left to CH3, double bonds up to O (all in a red box), and bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down, identified as HMG-CoA synthase (in blue). To the right is acetyl-CoA (in a blue box) [plus] H2O pointing down with a curved arrow to CoA-SH (in a blue box). Below the straight arrow is beta-hydroxy-beta-methylglutaryl-CoA (HMG-CoA), where C double bonds up and left to O, bonds down and left to –O, and bonds right to CH2 (all in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which bonds up to OH, down to CH3 (all in a red box), and right to CH2. CH2 bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and bonds down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down to acetoacetate, identified as HMG-CoA lyase (in blue). Another arrow jets out to the right to acetyl-CoA. Acetoacetate begins with C, which double bonds up and left to O, bonds down and left to –O, and bonds right to CH2 (all in a blue box), which bonds right to C, which double bonds up to O and bonds right to CH3 (all in a red box). Below acetoacetate an arrow points down and left to acetone, and reversible arrows point down and right to D-beta-hdroxybutyrate. The arrow pointing to acetone is identified as acetoacetate decarboxylase (in blue) and has an arrow jetting to the right pointing to CO2 (in a blue box). Acetone begins with C (in a pink box), which bonds left to CH3 (in a blue box), double bonds up to O and bonds right to CH3 (O, C, and CH3 are all in a pink box). The reversible arrows are identified as D-beta-hydroxybutyrate dehydrogenase (in blue), and to the left of the reversible arrows is a curved arrow pointing from NADH [plus] H+ to NAD+. D-beta-hydroxybutyrate begins with C double bonding up and left to O, bonding down and left to –O, and right to CH2 (all in a blue box), which bonds right to CH, which bonds up to OH and right to CH3 (all in a red box).
